previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, chronic chest and abdominal pain, and medication non-adherence was admitted for worsening left breast and chest pain, hypokalemia, and ongoing diarrhea due to C. difficile. She had not been taking her torsemide or metronidazole consistently. On admission, she had mild volume overload and low oxygen levels, which improved with IV furosemide and restarting oral diuretic therapy. Her potassium was repleted, and she was transitioned from oral metronidazole to liquid vancomycin for better adherence. Oral thrush was diagnosed and treated with nystatin. Her pain stabilized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with liquid formulations of key medications, clear instructions for anticoagulation monitoring, and a plan for outpatient follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  ___ DUP EXTEXT BIL (MAP/DVT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with bilateral lower extremity swelling, right
greater than left. Evaluate for DVT.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the bilateral lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow and augmentation of the bilateral common
femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins. Normal color flow and
compressibility are demonstrated in the posterior tibial and peroneal veins.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

There are bilateral ___ cysts.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the bilateral lower extremity veins.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with upper abd pain  // r/o infiltrate, abscess

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors most recent on ___.

FINDINGS: 

Heart size is normal.  The mediastinal and hilar contours are normal. The
pulmonary vasculature is normal.  There is a diffuse interstitial prominence. 
No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  No evidence of pulmonary edema.

IMPRESSION: 

Diffuse, mild interstitial abnormality could represent interstitial lung
disease or chronic heart failure.  No pulmonary edema.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ woman with upper abdominal pain.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT acquired axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained
after administration of 130 mL Omnipaque intravenous contrast. Enteric
contrast was not given. Coronal and sagittal reformats prepared and reviewed.

DOSE:  DLP:  843.94 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Mesenteric CTA from ___.  CTA chest from ___.

FINDINGS: 

CHEST:

A 5 mm nodular opacity at the right lung base, likely scarring, is stable
since ___ (series 2, image 8).  There is bilateral atelectasis at the lung
bases. There is no pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

 The liver enhances homogeneously, without concerning focal lesion. The
gallbladder and biliary tree are normal. The pancreas is normal, without focal
lesion or duct dilation. The spleen is normal in size, without focal lesion.
The adrenal glands are normal. The kidneys enhance normally and excrete
contrast briskly. There are no solid renal lesions.  There is mild bilateral
hydronephrosis without obstructing stone.  There is a sub cm hypodensity in
the upper pole the left kidney which is too small to characterize but
statistically likely a simple cyst (series 2, image 32). The stomach and
duodenum are normal. The small bowel and large bowel are normal in caliber,
without wall thickening or mass. There is pancolonic diverticulosis without
inflammatory changes.  The appendix is normal (series 2, image 54).

There is no intra- or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. There is no ascites,
fluid collection, or pneumoperitoneum. The abdominal aorta is normal caliber,
with patent main branches.  There is moderate atherosclerotic calcification of
the aorta and its major branches.  The portal vein and IVC are patent.

PELVIS:

The urinary bladder is without wall thickening or mass.  There is moderate
distention of the bladder. The rectum is unremarkable. There is no pelvic
mass. There is no free fluid. There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.
The uterus is not seen and may be surgically absent. There is no adnexal
abnormality bilaterally.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

There is no acute fracture. There are no destructive osseous lesions
concerning for malignancy or infection.  There are degenerative changes of the
spine as well as scoliosis.  There is a left total hip replacement. There are
no soft tissue masses.

IMPRESSION:


1. Pan-colonic diverticulosis without inflammatory changes.
2. Mild bilateral hydronephrosis without clear obstruction.  This may be the
result of chronic urinary outlet obstruction given the distended bladder.
